subject.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)

question: Should OpenClaw release a timed-out deferred-maintenance lane even though that permits a second same-session `ContextEngine.maintain()` call before the first plugin invocation settles?
rationale: This choice changes the permanent behavioral contract for external context-engine plugins and balances interactive-session liveness against compatibility with engines that assume one maintenance invocation per session.

options.title: Define a compatibility-preserving timeout lifecycle
options.body: Keep foreground turns unblocked but prevent a replacement maintenance invocation from reaching an existing engine until its prior invocation settles, or add an explicit additive cancellation/serialization contract first.

options.title: Accept concurrent plugin maintenance
options.body: Merge the documented requirement that all selected context engines must tolerate concurrent or re-entrant same-session `maintain()` calls after an opted-in timeout.

options.title: Pause this approach
options.body: Keep the reported stall tracked while maintainers choose a narrower liveness solution that does not change the existing plugin lifecycle.

recommendation.title: Define a compatibility-preserving timeout lifecycle
recommendation.body: Keep foreground turns unblocked but prevent a replacement maintenance invocation from reaching an existing engine until its prior invocation settles, or add an explicit additive cancellation/serialization contract first.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the current implementation and can supply the intended lifecycle details, while a repository owner should make the final public-contract decision.
